analysis:
The only changed lines in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (head 833-835) add `promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil` to the ProviderPromptContractPipeline call. Those lines fall outside the supplied excerpts (base text starts at 1018 and head text ends at about 529), so I could not read the call site or the receiving pipeline. The patch excerpt itself shows the call fully. The change looks like a hardening: it partitions a token-reuse or prompt-preparation cache by the same coordinator-authored scope as the prefix KV cache. When the coordinator supplies no authenticated scope (`cacheEnabled` false), it passes nil. This is consistent with T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle, SEC-035), which requires cacheSalt to be derived from the authenticated account and model build. The head text I did read shows `requestCacheScope` derived from `cacheScope`, with a diffusion-only local fallback (lines 442-443). `cacheEnabled` is false only for legacy coordinators with no authenticated scope (lines 108-110). I examined the base lines 1018-1552 and head lines 1-529 for behavior context (native MiMo media path, makeEventStream, release and cancellation). None of that text appears in the changed ranges.

Unverified contract: the receiving `ProviderPromptContractPipeline` is not supplied. Whether a nil scope disables token reuse entirely, or falls back to a shared global namespace, is not established. If nil falls back to a shared namespace, legacy coordinators would reintroduce cross-tenant prompt-token reuse. Also unverified: whether the scope is hashed or kept in memory only, and whether it is ever written to disk or logs. The next review pass should check the pipeline's handling of `promptCacheScope`, in particular nil semantics and whether the cache key includes the scope. A pipeline check is also needed to see whether any new at-rest or in-memory cache keeps prompt-derived material without scope isolation. I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence.
